source.title: Sparsity is the enemy of feature extraction (ft. absorption)

record.file_problem: Complete post text; not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: An analytical result shows that sparsity optimization can favor absorption in a simplified SAE, qualifying the idea that SAE features are complete representation units.
record.gate_note: The post derives reconstruction and sparsity results for a simplified untied SAE with a hierarchical pair of features. Its real-world SAE example and findings attributed to other papers are cited, not results produced by this post, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: An analytical proof sketch argues that sparsity optimization favors feature absorption, leaving holes in parent latents. This is a specific argument against SAE latents being complete units (V5), made in a simplified untied, bias-free SAE with orthogonal hierarchical features. It gives no measurement in trained SAEs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors show analytically that, in a simplified untied SAE, absorption leaves reconstruction intact while lowering sparsity loss, so sparsity optimization pushes toward absorption. From this they argue that SAE latents for safety-relevant concepts can't be trusted. They suggest Matryoshka SAEs, KL-based objectives, or parameter-space decomposition as remedies. They also expect absorption in all sparsity-based architectures, but they assert this rather than show it.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical proof sketch for feature absorption in a simplified untied SAE, rather than a reproduction of the original Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The sparsity benefit depends on p11>0, meaning datapoints with both hierarchical features occur; the derivation assumes mutually orthogonal unit-norm features and excludes the child-only case.

fits_no_version.finding: In the stated setup, every level of absorption δ gives exact reconstruction for the three allowed feature combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With hierarchical features, absorption is invisible to the reconstruction loss, so reconstruction cannot penalize it.

record.problems: Evidence is an analytical proof sketch under simplifying assumptions, not a measurement in trained SAEs or LLMs. The post's real-world example and reports of absorption come from cited work, not new results here.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. The cited real-world SAE examples and findings attributed to other papers were excluded because they are not results from this post.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy superposition of more features than dimensions. Features are assumed orthogonal.
All of it. The LLM absorption example (Gemma Scope latent 6510) is cited from Chanin et al., not produced here.

Stability and canonicality across runs or sizes. Whether trained SAEs actually reach absorbed solutions. Whether the argument holds in real models or for non-L1/Lp architectures (TopK and JumpReLU are only asserted).
All of it. Features are assumed to be 1-D unit vectors.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong proof sketch with no trained models. It shows the loss decreases along one hand-chosen absorption path, not that gradient descent finds that path or that it is the global optimum. The real-world example and the transcoder absorption finding are cited from other papers. The n/p notation is inconsistent, and the general sparsity formula only matches the stated latents at p=1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test superposition of more sparse features than dimensions, nearly orthogonal directions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test neurons sharing limited capacity or the proposed division between dedicated and shared dimensions.
Does not test polysemantic neurons arising for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The LLM example and reports of SAE absorption are attributed to other work; this post does not measure feature distribution or recovery in an LLM.
Tests incompleteness through absorption in a simplified hierarchical-feature setup, not feature stability over time or whether SAE features are canonical units in real models.
Assumes unit-norm mutually orthogonal feature vectors; does not compare one-dimensional with multidimensional features.

conditions.value: general amount; increasing δ lowers loss when p11>0

rows.locator: Sparsity under δ-absorption, General Case; Differentiating the Sparsity Loss
rows.note: The derivative is negative under the stated condition, so the sparsity objective favors increasing absorption.
rows.check: The general formula (2−δ)^(1/p) does not follow from the stated latents (z1=1−δ, z2=1) under a sum of |z|^p, except at p=1. The direction of the result holds for p≤1, but the closed form is the post's own and looks shaky. This caveat should be recorded.

relationships.condition: Simplified untied, bias-free SAE with orthogonal unit-norm features in a hierarchy f2⊂f1 and p11>0 (analytical, Lp sparsity penalty)
relationships.reason: Absorption leaves reconstruction exact while lowering sparsity loss (R2 vs R1). The sparsity gradient always favors more absorption (R3). So the sparsest solution's parent latent is incomplete. This is an argument, not a measured rate.
relationships.display_finding: Absorption kept reconstruction exact while lowering the sparsity loss, and the sparsity gradient always pushed toward more absorption, so the sparsest solution leaves the parent latent incomplete. This is an analytical argument, not a measured rate.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
